## Measured state 2026-09-05 ~18:50 — the "stalled 120 runs" premise no longer holds

Measured directly rather than inferred, because this ticket was about to be dispatched on its stated premise:

```
global rebar:  /Users/joeoakhart/.local/bin/rebar   mtime Sep  5 11:40   (~7h ago)
launchctl:     com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update    last exit status 0
               com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc   running (pid 75958)
               com.navapbc.rebar-serena-mirror-update   exit 0
uv:            /opt/homebrew/bin/uv        0.12.9  (Homebrew 2026-09-01)
               ~/.local/bin/uv             0.12.7
pipx:          nava-rebar 0.10.1
```

The updater is **reinstalling and exiting 0**, so the `required-version ==0.12.7` rejection loop described in the Root cause section is NOT currently firing. This corroborates the earlier comment that flagged the "stalled 119 runs" framing as in tension with observed evidence. The `UV_BIN` hardcoding may still be a latent defect — both uv builds are present and the ordering could invert again on the next Homebrew bump — but it is not producing a live stall right now. **Whoever claims this should re-derive the current failure mode before fixing the one in the description.**

## Direct evidence FOR AC4, obtained by failing to satisfy it manually

AC4 asks that "a stalled updater or an over-stale build is detectable locally". I attempted exactly that detection by hand and could not:

- `rebar --version` -> `Error: unknown subcommand '--version'`
- `~/.local/pipx/venvs/nava-rebar` exists, but has **no `direct_url.json`**, so the installed VCS commit is not recoverable from package metadata
- the only staleness signal available is the binary's **mtime**, which reports when the install last ran, NOT which commit it installed

So an operator (or an agent) currently has no way to answer "how far behind `origin/main` is the global build?" without reading updater logs that may have rotated. That is the gap AC4 names, demonstrated rather than asserted. The AC4 design already agreed with the operator — the LaunchAgent SELF-REPORTS a freshness signal rather than rebar inspecting LaunchAgent state — and this measurement supports that shape: what is missing is a durable, readable record of the installed commit, not a launchd probe.

## Disposition this tick

NOT dispatched. Reasons: the p1 urgency in the description is disproven by the measurement above; the remaining value is the AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5 detector work, whose file impact (`src/rebar/_commands/doctor*.py`, `src/rebar/llm/build_drift.py`) risks overlap with two agents currently working in `src/rebar/**`; and host capacity is committed to the duplicate-producer RCA (`anarchic-princely-raven`), which gates re-enabling the reconcile bridge.
